papers_read.title_as_printed: Pack text pdf/P-117.txt is the Rallabandi & Seetharaman MRI-PET fusion paper (BSPC 80 (2023) 104312), NOT the paper the record means. The record's '99.81% Acc' belongs to Aljalal et al., 'Mild cognitive impairment detection with optimally selected EEG channels based on variational mode decomposition and supervised machine learning', BSPC 87 (2024) 105462, PDF in the repository at downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S1746809423008959-main.pdf. Both read in full.

Linguistic-based Mild Cognitive Impairment detection using Informative Loss (Pourramezan Fard et al., Computers in Biology and Medicine 176 (2024) 108606); the record's claim_b cites P-11, a dedup stub of this same paper

what_each_reports.P-117: Resting-state 19-channel EEG, 61 participants (29 aMCI/32 HC), 10-fold CV over 3660 segment feature vectors; binary MCI vs HC accuracy 99.81% (11 NSGA-II channels, ensemble KNN).
what_each_reports.P-6: Transcript-based transformer on I-CONECT interviews, 68 subjects, subject-level 5-fold CV; binary MCI vs NC accuracy 85.16% (sd 5.76), AUC 84.75%.

quantity_a: Segment-level 10-fold CV accuracy, binary MCI vs HC, resting-state EEG, N=61
quantity_b: Subject-level 5-fold CV accuracy, binary MCI vs NC, conversational-language transcripts, N=68
incompatible_if_same: No: single cross-validated scores from unrelated methods and inputs; neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match: binary MCI vs cognitively normal
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Isfahan Noor Hospital EEG datasets vs I-CONECT
gates.validation_tier: match in tier (internal CV only) but segment-level vs subject-level folds
gates.modality_family: mismatch: EEG vs speech/language; no waiver

endpoint_and_metric: same metric type (accuracy) but different evaluation units and MCI definitions
performance_validity: flag applies to P-117 on the source (99.81%, internal CV, 61 participants, no external cohort)
independence: Independent groups and cohorts. The record is not independent of C-48: after the P-11 -> P-6 repoint it is the identical pair and claims.
grounds: This is the same pair as C-48 (claim_b's P-11 is a dedup stub of P-6); the modality-family and dataset-family gates fail with no waiver.
P-117's accuracy is computed over EEG segments and P-6's over subjects, so the evaluation units differ.
P-117 meets the performance-validity exclusion on its own PDF.
The pack PDF for P-117 is the wrong paper; the verdict uses the correct P-117 PDF found in the repository.

evidence_quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method. (correct PDF S1746809423008959)
For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. (correct PDF)
Since the number of available subjects in the I-CONECT dataset is 68, we assess the performance of our framework using the K-fold validation technique.
the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 85.16% and an AUC of 84.75%, with the corresponding std of 5.76 and 5.97, respectively.

record_defects: Duplicate record: identical to C-48 after the P-11 -> P-6 repoint; claim_b still names P-11 (a [STUB-DEDUP-OF-P-6] block).
The pack/paper_pdf_map entry for P-117 points to the wrong PDF (S1746809422007662); the correct PDF is S1746809423008959.
dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong; the bridging-evidence list does not bear on this pair.
